blocks.explanation:
Remove \(1 - \sin x\) from the denominator by multiplying by \(1 + \sin x\).
Plan: the integrand becomes \(x(\sec^2 x + \sec x\tan x)\); integrate by parts with \(x\) first.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{x}{1 - \sin x}\,dx\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: multiply by \(\frac{1 + \sin x}{1 + \sin x}\); then integration by parts with \(x\) first and \(\sec^2 x + \sec x\tan x\) second.

Rationalise the denominator
\[\dfrac{x}{1 - \sin x}\cdot\dfrac{1 + \sin x}{1 + \sin x} = \dfrac{x(1 + \sin x)}{\cos^2 x}\]
\[= x(\sec^2 x + \sec x\tan x)\]
Why: \(1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\); \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = \sec x\tan x\).

Integration by parts
\[\int (\sec^2 x + \sec x\tan x)\,dx = \tan x + \sec x\]
\[= x(\tan x + \sec x) - \int (\tan x + \sec x)\,dx\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{dx}\tan x = \sec^2 x\), \(\frac{d}{dx}\sec x = \sec x\tan x\).

Standard integrals
\[= x\tan x + x\sec x - \ln|\sec x|\]
\[\quad - \ln|\sec x + \tan x| + c\]
Why: \(\int \tan x\,dx = \ln|\sec x|\), \(\int \sec x\,dx = \ln|\sec x + \tan x|\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}[x(\tan x + \sec x)] = \tan x + \sec x + x(\sec^2 x + \sec x\tan x)\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}[\ln|\sec x| + \ln|\sec x + \tan x|] = \tan x + \sec x\]
Why: the difference is \(x(\sec^2 x + \sec x\tan x) = \frac{x}{1 - \sin x}\).
blocks.final_answer: \(x\tan x + x\sec x - \ln|\sec x| - \ln|\sec x + \tan x| + c\)
